key_insight: The paper learns Koopman embeddings directly from data with a kernel-based autoencoder trained via bilevel optimization, avoiding the need to predefine a feature dictionary.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a scalable and more interpretable alternative to neural autoencoders for linearizing nonlinear dynamics in forecasting and system identification.
method: Combine collocation ideas with bilevel optimization.
Jointly learn a kernel dictionary and its Koopman approximation.
Use EDMD-kDL to compute finite-dimensional Koopman embeddings from data.
evidence_signal: In experiments on tasks including global sea-surface-temperature forecasting and video data, EDMD-kDL matched or outperformed ANN-based methods while scaling better than standard kernel approaches.
watch_item: Performance depends on the choice of collocation points and kernel design, which can affect stability, accuracy, and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
